title: Is alignment depth correlated with model size within a single model family?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: if alignment scales with model size, small deployed models are disproportionately vulnerable. If not, scaling is not a solution to shallow alignment and new training objectives are required. Both outcomes directly guide safety investment decisions.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: KL divergence computation across model size variants is straightforward with reference code. Loading models of varying sizes on Colab Pro requires memory management but is documented. Simple linear regression is basic statistics. Guided with mentor support.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: compute alignment depth per model size within one family, plot depth vs log(parameters), run regression. Single deliverable: a scatter plot with regression line. Minimal dependencies, clear success criteria.

novelty.reasoning: While scaling patterns in adversarial alignment have been studied (arXiv:2511.13788 found correlation between attacker size and harm), and alignment depth theory exists (Markov chain perspective, arXiv:2502.00669), the specific question of whether alignment depth (KL divergence metric from Qi et al.) scales with model size within a single family has not been directly investigated. Existing work focuses on adversarial robustness scaling or theoretical depth analysis, not empirical depth measurement across size variants. The proposed scatter plot of depth vs log(parameters) within one family is a clean, novel empirical contribution.

evidence: Qi et al. (2024). Safety Alignment Should Be Made More Than Just a Few Tokens Deep. ICLR 2025.
Scaling Patterns in Adversarial Alignment. arXiv:2511.13788.
